new_statements.quote: Medefaidrin has a phonology with plausible conventional syllable phonotactics Adams (1947:26). Unlike the enclaving Ibibio, which is a tone language, Medefaidrin is a stress language, though apparently adaptation to Ibibio is taking place. [...] several features which are strikingly English-like: complex syllables which are more English-like than Ibibio-like; stress-based prosody rather than tone-based prosody; SVO word order like English
new_statements.citation: Gibbon, Dafydd; Ekpenyong, Moses; Urua, Eno-Abasi. 2010. Medefaidrin: resources documenting the birth and death language life-cycle. Proceedings of LREC 2010, Valletta, pp. 2702-2708 (ELRA). DOI 10.63317/3gzkfcbb48ep
new_statements.locator: §6.2.1 Phonology, p. 2706 (PDF p. 5); also §7 Conclusion, p. 2707
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (Gibbon, Ekpenyong & Urua 2010, LREC, 7 pp., text layer). PDF p. 5 = printed p. 2706, §6.2.1 Phonology, reads verbatim: "Medefaidrin has a phonology with plausible conventional syllable phonotactics Adams (1947:26). Unlike the enclaving Ibibio, which is a tone language, Medefaidrin is a stress language, though apparently adaptation to Ibibio is taking place." The second quoted segment is verbatim at §7 Conclusion, p. 2707: "several features which are strikingly English-like: complex syllables which are more English-like than Ibibio-like; stress-based prosody rather than tone-based prosody; SVO word order like English". The report's locator (p. 2706) is right; the line saying p. 2705…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is described as a stress (non-tonal) language, in contrast to the surrounding tone language Ibibio, with a note that it is apparently adapting toward Ibibio prosody; no source opened states which syllable of the word carries stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the caveat that 'adaptation to Ibibio is taking place' (WOCAL 2009 slide 52: 'stress (though apparently yielding to Ibibio)'), i.e. the stress system may be giving way to tone under contact.
new_statements.domain_note: Type statement only (stress-based vs tone-based prosody); no word-level placement, no examples with stress marks in the paper, slides or lexicon extract. The claim is attributed to Adams (1947:26), which could not be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog mede1238 'Medefidrin' = ISO 639-3 [dmf] Medefaidrin, the constructed liturgical 'spirit language' of the Obɛri Ɔkaimɛ (Oberi Okaime) church near Itu, Akwa Ibom State (Glottolog family 'Speech Register'). All sources describe the same variety; the enclaving natural language is Ibibio (ibib1240), a tone language, and the sources say Medefaidrin prosody is drifting toward it.
